data.title: Chinese Firms Going Global Now Compete on Trust, Not Just Value for Money, YeePay’s Global CEO Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 20 -- For Chinese companies going global, competition no longer focuses on value for money, as it has shifted toward long-term, sustainable cross-border trust, according to the global chief executive officer of Chinese cross-border payment services provider YeePay.

Chinese firms expanding overseas are no longer simply rushing to grab market share but now want to put down roots, Terry Hua told Yicai in a recent interview. Cross-border payments are like taking the pulse of trade, as shifts in orders, corporate concerns, and market opportunities show up first in the flow of funds, he noted.

While large enterprises look at their global footprints, small- and medium-sized merchants care more about fund security, cost control, and local compliance, Hua explained.

For example, small Chinese businesses expanding into Southeast Asia have good products, but they are worried about getting paid, Hua said. Local-currency settlement runs through complex, multi-step channels, funds arrive slowly, and exchange-rate losses can erode profits at any time. If the funding chain is unstable, merchants dare not scale up, even after receiving orders.

"Emerging markets present great opportunities for global businesses, but payment complexity remains a major barrier," Hua pointed out. YeePay continues to invest in local-currency capabilities, combining real-time foreign exchange conversion with intelligent payment routing.

YeePay operates through licensed or regulated entities in China’s Hong Kong special administrative region, the United States, Mexico, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, according to Hua. Its platform supports payment services in more than 200 countries and regions, with real-time foreign exchange covering over 100 currencies.

During the Singapore FinTech Festival, YeePay signed memoranda of understanding with Thailand's Kasikornbank, Luxembourg’s Banking Circle, and South Korea’s GLN International, expanded its partnerships with UK-based ClearBank, which became its safeguarding bank in the UK and Europe in April, and partnered with Singapore-based treasury and payment platform Finmo.

The company also showcased its Global Enterprise Account, Pay to China, intelligent FX management, and local-currency collection and payout services for emerging markets at the Singapore FinTech Festival, which runs from Nov. 18 to today, concurrently with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

Bilateral Trade via Small Currencies

Inclusive growth in Asia-Pacific should not be just for large economies and big companies, Hua said to Yicai.

Since YeePay built small-currency settlement channels to China, local merchants have been able to trade with China more smoothly, currency conversion losses have fallen sharply, and distinctive products that once struggled to reach Chinese consumers can now enter the market directly, he explained.

Trade runs both ways, Hua believes. Chinese consumers can get distinctive goods, while farmers and small businesses in smaller economies can earn a steady income.

“Technology alone does not define competitiveness in payments,” YeePay’s President and co-founder Chen Yu said at a panel on how artificial intelligence is reshaping global payments attended by executives from J.P. Morgan, Standard Chartered, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation, and Visa. “A deep understanding of industry needs and merchants' real-world challenges is equally essential."

YeePay is building payment infrastructure for two-way expansion, helping Chinese companies reach global markets while making China and the wider Asia-Pacific region more accessible to overseas businesses, Chen noted.

APEC has been pushing to connect business environments across Asia-Pacific, Hua said, adding that financial infrastructure is the foundation that lets small businesses dare to go abroad and survive.

YeePay aims to provide more than payment channels, a resilient funding network that helps Chinese companies take root in Asia-Pacific and close the gaps in their funding chains, according to Hua.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China Has Become Ingka Centres’ Innovation Hub After Years of Learning, Exec Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Ingka Centres drew on the experiences from other markets to set up business in China nearly 20 years ago, but after all this time, the Swedish shopping centers operator’s Chinese team has become the key driver of global innovation, according to the managing director of Ingka Centres.

When Ingka Centres established its Chinese business, it used the knowledge from other markets, such as the United States, Europe, Thailand, and Malaysia, to “bring a cocktail of the best pieces and put it together,” Sebastian Hylving told Yicai in an interview yesterday. “But over the years, this has changed.”

Now, Ingka Centres sees China and the local team as its innovation hub where the future is, Hylving explained. “Now we can take the lessons and advancements we have in China and bring them to Europe.”

For example, Ingka Centres has teamed up with Chinese unmanned logistics vehicle maker Neolix Technology and Dishangtie Car Rental, a Chinese electric vehicle leasing company that counts Ingka Group as one of its investors, to jointly develop autonomous retail vehicles. Both Ingka Centres and Ikea are part of Ingka Group.

The self-driving retail vehicles pick up products from brands at Ingka Centres’meeting places and deliver them autonomously to parks, at the foot of mountains for hikers, or to elderly care homes for residents who cannot easily move around, Hylving said. The company will run tests in China and later consider bringing the vehicles to Europe or the US.

China is changing faster than any other market, Hylving said. “I don't see that speed anywhere else, even in other parts of Asia.”

Hylving arrived in China when Ingka set up shop in 2008 and lived there until 2014, when he moved to Southeast Asia. The company has invested more than CNY27 billion (USD4 billion) in the Chinese market since 2009, according to Hylving.

In 2008, China had department stores and hypermarkets rather than real shopping malls, so Ingka Centres brought Livat to give people reasons to visit beyond shopping. Ingka Centres now calls Livat shopping malls meeting places, “living rooms for local communities.”

The company does not view a mall as just an item on the balance sheet, but tries to understand what people in the community need and want, Hylving explained.

In China, Livat welcomed about 150 million visitors last year, including 36.4 million to Livat Beijing, Hylving said. Globally, Ingka Centres received more than 330 million visitors in fiscal 2026, up from 320 million a year earlier.

Much of traditional, transactional shopping can be replaced by a click online, but people still need to meet in person. "We like to be with other people, we like to see, and we like to be seen," Hylving pointed out.

Ingka Centres' latest Play Forward: Life in Communities report found that six in 10 people feel they play less than they did a decade ago, while three in four say play is important for emotional connection. Online brands are also moving offline to get noticed. Online, "you meet everyone, but you also meet no one," he said.

Looking ahead three to five years, Hylving said that the biggest opportunities in China will come from the local team's ongoing effort to understand customers, services, stores, and events, while keeping meeting places clean, safe, and efficient to run.

As for artificial intelligence, Hylving believes it will bring many opportunities, but also challenges. What matters is keeping a positive outlook and acting on it, he added.

Ingka Centres’ Deal With China’s GoHigh Is ‘Routing Asset Rotation’

In December last year, Ingka Centres announced it would team up with Chinese investment firm GoHigh Capital to establish a real estate fund that will co-own three of its longest-operating Livat meeting places in Beijing, Wuhan, and Wuxi.

The deal means Ingka Centres will continue to manage and operate the meeting places under the Livat brand. Ingka Group's fiscal 2026 results, released on Nov. 17, confirmed that the three meeting places have been transferred to the co-owned fund.

The partnership frees up capital for future growth and brings the company closer to local partners, Hylving explained. 

He called this deal a routine asset rotation. “We hadn't done a rotation in China before,” he noted. “It's a natural part of our business model.”

Partners are drawn to Ingka Centres not only because of the assets, but because of its local team's knowledge of the market and its customers, Hylving said.

data.title: China’s Xingyun Technology to Provide Client With Up to USD300 Million of AI Tokens
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Xingyun Technology, a Chinese firm that launched an artificial intelligence “token factory” business earlier this year, has agreed a five-year deal potentially worth as much as CNY2 billion (USD300 million) to supply a Hong Kong-based property manager with AI tokens.

Xingyun will supply the tokens to New Silkroad Holding Group through application programming interface calls, mainly for its business operations in South Korea, with billing based on actual usage, the Changsha-based company announced late yesterday. The initial order is worth CNY200 million (USD30 million).

The agreement will support Xingyun’s business transformation, help it to penetrate overseas markets, broaden the commercial use of its AI tokens, and provide tokens for producing film and television content, such as short videos, online dramas, and digital humans, aimed at mainstream audiences, it said.

New Silkroad could also use the tokens in other lines of business, including the research and development of functional foods, AI-driven farm animal breeding, and global trade, Xingyun added. Specific service details will be set out in subsequent orders.

Xingyun, formerly known as cross-border e-commerce business Youkeshu Technology, went through a court-supervised bankruptcy reorganization between 2024 and last year that saved it from a stock market delisting and transformed it into a AI computing-power provider.

The company’s computing-power business has grown rapidly, supported by its global cross-border supply chain network and diversified server procurement channels, providing a solid foundation for fulfilling the contract with New Silkroad, Xingyun pointed out. Its token factory’s first computing nodes should be ready to provide services by June 30 next year, it said.

New Silkroad owns 55 percent of the Glorious Hill project, a resort complex under development on Jeju Island, South Korea. Last month, the company completed a minority equity investment in i-Aurora and &SOUL, two South Korean firms operating an ecosystem for global K-Pop fans.

Xingyun’s shares [SHE: 300209] closed 3.5 percent down at CNY21.38 (USD3.20) each in Shenzhen today, after surging by more than 17 percent yesterday afternoon. New Silkroad [HKG: 00472] rose 2.6 percent to 19.5 Hong Kong cents (2 US cents) today.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Tencent, ByteDance Tout AI Office App Gains as User Numbers Surge
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Chinese tech giants Tencent Holdings and ByteDance have reported strong user growth and substantial revenue from their artificial intelligence office assistants as competition in China's AI productivity market heats up.

Tencent's WorkBuddy had more than 10 million daily active users as of early November, while ByteDance's Doubao Work surpassed eight million, according to figures released yesterday.

Beyond attracting users, both companies are beginning to generate substantial revenue from their AI tools, raising the stakes for rivals including Alibaba Group Holding.

WorkBuddy's annualized revenue, calculated using its latest seven days of sales, has exceeded USD500 million, double that of video-call tool Tencent Meeting, which launched seven years ago, Tencent President Martin Lau said during an earnings conference call yesterday following the release of the company's third-quarter results.

The AI assistant's revenue in the quarter ended in September was also more than five times that of the previous quarter, Lau added.

WorkBuddy consumed an average of more than 100 trillion tokens a day as of early November, making it Tencent's AI application with the highest daily token consumption, the Shenzhen-based company said in its third-quarter earnings report.

ByteDance is also making headway with corporate customers. The Beijing-based company said Doubao Work had generated over CNY2 billion (USD300 million) in annual recurring revenue from businesses within three months of its launch.

Tech Giants Tap Existing Platforms to Expand AI Reach

Rather than building their AI office businesses from scratch, the three companies are tapping their existing platforms to attract users.

ByteDance developed Doubao Work by integrating its Doubao AI assistant with its workplace collaboration platform Lark.

Tencent has leveraged the user base of its WeChat social media application to expand WorkBuddy's reach and incorporated third-party AI models, including DeepSeek, into the assistant.

Alibaba, meanwhile, has been developing its Qwen AI assistant for enterprise customers, drawing on its DingTalk workplace collaboration platform.

The stakes are rising as China's broader AI agent market expands. The market reached CNY80.4 billion (USD12.1 billion) last year, more than doubling from a year earlier, according to a report released by iiMedia Research. It could reach CNY696.8 billion (USD104.5 billion) by 2030, the research firm forecast.

Unlike traditional office software, AI office assistants primarily attract individuals, but enterprise customers offer another avenue for growth, iiMedia noted. Developers could tap both markets by offering lightweight tools to individuals and tailored solutions to businesses, creating multiple revenue streams, the research firm suggested.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Emmi Laine

data.title: Roche Completes USD300 Million Shanghai Plant, Eyes Local Production of Eye Drug by 2028
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Roche has finished construction of a CNY2 billion (USD300 million) biopharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Shanghai, marking a major step in the Swiss pharmaceutical giant’s efforts to expand local production of innovative medicines in China.

The facility, which is Roche’s second innovative drug manufacturing base in the country, is expected to begin local production of faricimab, an injectable treatment for retinal diseases such as macular degeneration, by mid-2028 with sterile filling operations scheduled to start by the end of 2030, the Basel-based company said yesterday.

This will mark the first time a multinational pharmaceutical company has achieved localized production of large-molecule antibody-based biopharmaceuticals in China, it added.

Faricimab, which is marketed as Vabysmo, is the world's first bispecific antibody that targets both vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2), helping to inhibit abnormal blood vessel growth while improving vascular stability. The drug was approved in China in December 2023 and added to the National Reimbursement Drug List in 2025.

Roche became the first multinational pharmaceutical firm to move into the Zhangjiang High-Tech Park in Shanghai in 1994. After 30 years of development, Roche now has 28 products on the market in China, covering eight fields such as oncology, infectious diseases, neuroscience and ophthalmology, according to its website.

Over the next two to five years, Roche plans to submit nearly 20 new products with more than 40 new indications for regulatory approval in China, it said. These will cover a range of therapeutic areas, including oncology and hematology, neuroscience, immunology, ophthalmology as well as cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases.

Going forward, Roche will use the new manufacturing facility to further prioritize local production and accelerate the rollout of more locally manufactured innovative medicines in China, including treatments for breast cancer, lung cancer and infectious diseases, it added.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: China Adds Record 51 Innovative Drugs to Reimbursement List, But Hospital Access Barriers Persist
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- China has added 51 Category 1 innovative drugs to its recently released 2026 National Reimbursement Drug List, the largest annual increase on record. However, inclusion on the list does not guarantee that the medicine will reach patients, as several hurdles remain before they can be stocked by hospital pharmacies, industry insiders told Yicai.

Before a new drug can be stocked by a hospital pharmacy, it must undergo a review by the hospital’s pharmaceutical affairs committee, the insiders said. The hospital must also complete arrangements with the drug supplier and distribution service provider, enter the drug’s code into its information system, and train doctors in the relevant clinical departments on how to use it. All these procedures take time.

The National Reimbursement Drug List adds a large number of medicines every year, but not all of them automatically make their way into every hospital pharmacy, said the head of the pharmacy department at a leading public hospital. Hospitals are also extremely cautious about bringing in new medicines because removing a drug once it has been added to their formularies can be very difficult, they added.

Whether to admit an innovative drug depends on several factors, the insiders said. Hospitals need to assess whether there is sufficient patient demand, whether the new medicine offers significant therapeutic improvements over existing treatments and whether its clinical benefits justify adding it to the hospital’s formulary. They must also consider whether introducing high-priced innovative drugs could push their total medical insurance reimbursement claims beyond regulatory limits.

In addition, regulations prohibit hospitals from earning commissions on the drugs they sell. This means expensive innovative medicines become a cost burden as soon as they enter hospital pharmacies. Many innovative drugs are biologics and, once introduced, hospitals must bear a range of associated costs, including cold-chain storage, the insiders said.

Hospital Incentives

To address hospitals' concerns about introducing innovative medicines, the National Health Commission and three other government departments issued a notice earlier this month requiring major public medical institutions to improve their procedures and workflows for admitting innovative drugs and to promptly include them in their formularies.

The notice also stipulated that the use of innovative drugs will be excluded from a range of performance evaluation indicators for public medical institutions.

This removes some of the justifications hospitals have used to keep innovative drugs out, said Jin Chunlin, director of the Shanghai Health Development Research Center. It also addresses a key concern among hospitals, which is that they must bear the financial losses associated with using innovative medicines themselves.

However, as long as the compensation mechanism for public hospitals remains unchanged, hospital presidents and department heads will have little financial incentive to introduce innovative drugs, Jin said.

The new policy may make it harder for hospitals to block innovative medicines from entering their facilities, but additional positive incentives are needed to encourage hospitals and doctors to actively promote their use, he added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: CAAM to Scrutinize Supplier Payment Practices at Major Chinese Carmakers
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 17 -- The China Association of Automobile Manufacturers will evaluate supplier payment practices at 17 major domestic carmakers, including BYD and SAIC Motor, at the request of regulators seeking to standardize payment practices, shorten payment terms and promote the healthy development of the automotive industry.

CAAM has been commissioned by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology to conduct the assessment as an independent third-party organization, the industry association said yesterday. The companies under review include leading automakers such as BYD, SAIC, Dongfeng Motor Group, FAW Group and Geely Auto, as well as emerging electric vehicle manufacturers such as Xiaomi Auto, Li Auto, Nio and Xpeng.

The evaluation will be conducted annually and cover several areas, including whether automakers pay suppliers within 60 days, maintain long-term and stable supplier relationships and have built clear and effective accounts payable management systems, CAAM said. It will also examine compliance in aspects such as the proportion of payments made in cash and negotiation mechanisms.

Data will be collected through a combination of regular reporting by carmakers and random checks of selected suppliers, it said. Auto manufacturers must submit reports on their supplier payment practices for the previous calendar year by Jan. 31 each year, followed by reports covering the first half of the current year by July 31.

Over the past few years, intensifying competition in China’s automotive industry has led to increasingly extended supplier payment terms, putting pressure on the healthy development of the broader industry. Against this backdrop, 17 major Chinese carmakers jointly pledged in June last year to keep supplier payment terms within 60 days. CAAM subsequently issued an industry initiative calling on automakers to standardize their payment practices.

In September, the MIIT and the State Administration for Market Regulation rolled out new regulations aimed at standardizing carmakers’ payments to suppliers and improving payment-term management. This effectively elevated what had previously been a voluntary industry self-regulatory initiative into a formal regulatory requirement.

Over the past year, average payment terms among China’s major automakers have shortened significantly, while the proportion of payments in cash has significantly increased, resulting in an overall improvement in payment practices.

However, supplier payments involve multiple stages and practices vary considerably among carmakers. Significant challenges remain in further optimizing payment terms, and Chinese vehicle manufacturers still have room for improvement compared with established multinational automakers, an MIIT official said.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese Business Jet Market Grows Driven by Demand From Execs, Rich People
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Business jets have become increasingly popular in China since corporate executives and high-net-worth individuals have begun to view private jets as an on-demand travel service for routine use.

The number of domestic and international business jet flights in China rose nearly 10 percent to 14,264 in the first half of the year from a year earlier, with international business jet flights up 17 percent to 6,833, according to data from Flight Master.

Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport had handled 400 business jet flights this year as of Nov. 13, a 45 percent increase from the same period last year, according to data from the airport in China’s southern Guangzhou.

Large companies and their management teams, private entrepreneurs, multinational corporations, and high-net-worth individuals are the main drivers of demand for business aviation services in China, according to Yitong Business Aviation Management, a provider of ground services for business jet flights.

“Business travel has become an important case scenario for business jets,” a staffer at Yitong Business Aviation told Yicai.

“For example, a manufacturing company with production bases in multiple cities may need its management team to travel quickly to different regions to inspect factories, visit clients, and conduct project negotiations,” the staffer said. “Business jets offer them a new travel option that is not constrained by commercial flight schedules while also providing a comfortable travel experience.”

Moreover, as Chinese companies accelerate overseas investment, build production bases abroad, and expand into international markets, cross-border travel demand from corporate executives, project management teams, and staff at investment institutions is also rising, the staffer added.

For clients who travel frequently, business jets help improve the efficiency of business activities, especially when a single trip must cover multiple destinations or when the project location lacks convenient commercial flight options.

For executives at Chinese new energy vehicle, power battery, advanced manufacturing, and pharmaceutical companies that are going global, business jets provide an efficient and comfortable means of transportation for overseas investment inspections and for the dispatch of personnel to manage overseas factories, supply chains, and projects, the staffer said.

China’s four first-tier cities -- Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen -- are important hubs for China’s business aviation market, but other economically vibrant cities, such as Hangzhou, Chengdu, and Chongqing, have also developed relatively strong demand for business jets, according to Yitong Business Aviation.

Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia are among the more active destinations for cross-border business-jet travel from Chinese mainland.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China Cuts US Treasury Holdings in September to Lowest Level in Over 18 Years
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- China, the United States’ third-largest creditor, cut its holdings of US Treasury bonds for the fourth consecutive month in September to the lowest since July 2008.

China’s holdings of US Treasuries fell by USD27 billion to about USD564 billion in September from the previous month, according to data released by the US Department of the Treasury yesterday.

The United Kingdom overtook China as the US’ second-largest creditor in March 2025, and the standings have not changed since then. The UK cut its holdings of US Treasuries by USD8.7 billion to about USD986 billion in September from August.

The total foreign holdings of US Treasury bonds fell by USD75.5 billion to USD9.24 trillion in September from the month before, the lowest in a year. The US Treasury index fell 2.2 percent in the period, as the Federal Reserve launched a new round of rate hikes to curb inflation.

Japan, the US’ largest creditor, also trimmed its US Treasuries holdings by USD5.2 billion to USD1.063 trillion in September, the lowest since the end of 2024. Japanese authorities took measures this summer to support the sharply weakened yen. Data shows that Tokyo sold some securities, including US Treasuries, to help finance its unprecedented foreign exchange intervention.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Jinluo Has No Comment on Rumors DCP Capital Will Buy Chinese Meat Giant for USD2 Billion
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Jinluo Group said to refer only to information on its website in response to Yicai's inquiry about whether rumors that Chinese private equity firm DCP Capital will acquire the leading meat processor for USD2 billion are true.

In addition, workers from DCP Capital told Yicai they knew nothing about such a deal.

Online rumors claimed Jinluo and DCP Capital are in talks for the former to sell its main businesses, including meat processing, sausages, and cold fresh meat, but not all of its assets. ‌‌

Linyi-based Jinluo is one of China's top three ham sausage brands, mainly focusing on pig slaughtering and deep processing of meat products and soybeans, according to its website. Last year, its operating revenue of CNY30.9 billion (USD4.6 billion) ranked it among the top 500 private firms in the country.

The ham sausage market has been shrinking in recent years, with no sign of a short-term recovery, so it may be the best time for Jinluo to sell its business, Zhu Ruishi, director at King Bird Strategic Consulting, said to Yicai. Giving up its ham sausage business suggests the firm has a clear plan for the future and may see potential in other businesses, Zhu pointed out.

In 2014, rumors circulated that Jinluo was in contact with state-owned China Oil and Foodstuffs over an acquisition, followed by reports in 2023 that China Resources Holdings planned to buy it for CNY12 billion (USD1.8 billion). The involved parties denied both.

Established in 2017, DCP Capital has invested in COFCO Joycome Foods, Simple Love Yogurt‌, Adopt a Cow, and other brands, according to corporate data platform Tianyancha. Its core team has led KKR and Morgan Stanley's private equity investment business in Asia, its website showed.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China's Pre-Owned Home Sales by Area Rise 11.4% in First 10 Months
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- The sales area of second-hand homes across China jumped 11.4 percent in the first 10 months of this year after months of consecutive growth, setting the domestic real estate market on track to gradually stabilize.

Pre-owned home sales by area rose 10.7 percent in the first nine months of this year from a year ago after climbing 10.6 percent in the January to August period, according to the latest data from the National Bureau of Statistics. For last month, the year-on-year growth was 18.9 percent, compared with 11.5 percent in September, Zhongtai Securities said in a research note.

Resale property deals accounted for more than half of China's housing turnover in the first half of this year, with that share climbing to 52.6 percent last month from 52.2 percent in September.

Chinese developers will curb land acquisition spending, with a sharp drop in land outlays expected next year and the year after, following the latest property regulatory rules that have extended their cash collection cycle by 12 to 15 months, said Shi Lulu, director of Asia-Pacific corporate ratings at Fitch Ratings. Industry observers expect a further decline in new homes supply and sales through 2028, she added.

The impact of these supply-side shifts on overall house sales will likely start to materialize in the second half of next year, Shi noted, adding that saleable asset inventories secured by developers before the new rules took effect on Aug. 28 will gradually run down by late 2027. Tighter presale requirements for newly acquired projects may then drive a deeper contraction in sales than this year, she pointed out.

Constrained new home supply will divert some demand to the resale market, which will in turn underpin second-hand home prices. Benefits will be unevenly distributed across the market, with build quality and supporting amenities remaining core performance drivers at prime locations.

Second-hand home sales made up 52 percent of total house sales in the first eight months of this year, Shi noted. Drawing parallels with mature property markets in Japan, South Korea, and the United States, she expects the ratio to climb to 60 percent to 65 percent around 2028–2029.

Improving quality of new homes and the rising share of second-hand house sales bode well for a gradual stabilization of the sector, putting the market on a path of steady, sound, and high-quality development, said Hu Xiaoyu, real estate analyst at China Galaxy Securities.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China Takes Steps to Speed Up Third-Generation Nuclear Power Rollout
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- China is seeking to accelerate the introduction of its proprietary third-generation nuclear power technology by improving reactor design, digitizing project management, speeding up equipment production, and harmonizing technical standards. The push also involves bringing private investors into projects to widen the funding base and bolster the domestic supply chain.

China General Nuclear Power Group unveiled the Hualong One 2.0, a third-generation pressurized water reactor, in September, featuring improvements in safety, cost-effectiveness, and technological performance.

The upgraded reactor design is intended to boost the efficiency of both project management and construction by 20 percent, with the overall building period capped at 54 months, according to Kan Shuo, deputy director of the Project Management Engineering Technology Support Centre at China Nuclear Engineering Corporation.

At the end of last year, the generating capacity of nuclear power units in commercial operation in China was 62.5 million kilowatts, less than 2 percent of the nation’s total electricity production capacity. This leaves a significant gap to cover to reach the 200-million-kilowatt target projected by the China Nuclear Energy Association for 2040.

Addressing the pressure to meet delivery timelines, Kan noted that in February, China National Nuclear Corporation proposed integrating digital engineering concepts into the design-and-construction process. This allows for seamless flow of data across different project sectors, with the goal of achieving a 20 percent improvement in both management and construction efficiency, and capping the total project duration at 54 months.

The initial delivery estimate for a Hualong One 2.0 reactor was nearly 50 months, said Liu Chang, project management director at First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power & Petrochemical, a firm responsible for equipment manufacturing. But through process refinement, the delivery time is now expected to be just over 40 months, Liu noted.

Private Capital

In terms of capital, China has begun introducing private investment into nuclear power projects. The San'ao Nuclear Power Plant in Zhejiang province is the first to have private equity participation. The plant is set to have six 1,000-megawatt Hualong One units, with a total projected investment of CNY120 billion (USD17.9 billion).
 

Private investors have a 2 percent stake in the project's first phase, a figure that rises to 30 percent by the third phase, setting a record for the most private funding in China’s nuclear power sector. 

"The participation of private capital has become a key prerequisite for the approval of certain nuclear power projects,” said Xu Lingbin, deputy manager of general management at Cangnan Nuclear Power, which is responsible for building and running the San'ao Nuclear Power Plant.

“Private capital helps supplement the substantial equity funding required for these projects, and private enterprises with strong industrial backgrounds can foster synergy across the upstream and downstream supply chains," Xu told Yicai.

Unified Standards

Efforts are also underway to harmonize standards to facilitate faster project implementation. China’s two major nuclear power conglomerates, CGN and CNNC, previously used different technical standards. 

Efforts to harmonize standards began in 2017, but the alignment did not include a number of equipment components. As of 2024, atomic power industry regulators have pushed for further standardization, encompassing the entire project lifecycle, from design and construction to operation and decommissioning. 

"Promoting the unification of standards is a positive development for the manufacturing sector,” said Gao Dianbao, executive deputy general manager of First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power, which supplies equipment to both CGN and CNNC. “It streamlines processes and helps unlock production capacity," Gao added.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Tencent’s Capex to Remain at Peak Levels Through 2027
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 19 -- Tencent Holdings’ capital expenditure will peak this year and remain at that level over the next year amid heavy investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure, but the Chinese internet giant is expected to see a significant improvement in financial performance from 2028 onward.

Capex payments were abnormally high in the second and third quarters this year, but with Tencent securing long-term contracts, cash outflows from prepayments will decline and some quarters may even see reversals, James Mitchell said at an earnings call late yesterday. Cash capex, or prepayments, has already peaked and may fluctuate around peak levels for the rest of this year and through 2027, followed by likely declines, he noted.

President Martin Lau added that the infrastructure being built is mainly to launch AI-native businesses and, once finished, can be used to continuously train new generations of models and generate tokens. Therefore, when capex commitments for this year and the next are completed, Tencent will be able to use the already-built infrastructure in 2028, leading to a marked improvement in its financial performance, he pointed out.

Based on non-international financial reporting standards, Tencent’s operating profit fell 6 percent to CNY68.1 billion (USD10.2 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from a year earlier, while its revenue rose 8 percent to CNY207.3 billion (USD31.1 billion), according to its financial report. Capex surged 527 percent to CNY81.4 billion, with capex payments of CNY65.1 billion.

In addition, equipment prices have been elevated this year and will remain so in 2027, but are expected to fall substantially in 2028, Lau said, adding that in the course of model training and inference, computing efficiency is doubling year by year, meaning the same facilities will deliver higher training efficiency and greater token output in the future.

Impact of Advanced Chip Supply Restrictions

Investment in AI infrastructure involves buying advanced chips, so Tencent’s management also addressed the impact of supply restrictions.

The restrictions are a hurdle for all domestic players, and whether they rent or build computing power overseas, the advanced compute available has been reduced, Lau noted. Training will be affected, so Tencent’s next-generation model may take longer to release, he added.

However, in the long run, China’s supply chain is expected to mature and catch up, and on the AI inference side, since the models are highly efficient, the domestic supply chain is fully capable of supporting them, he pointed out. All Chinese players will likely eventually rely on domestically produced supply chains and chips, he stressed.

According to Mitchell, domestic chips can already run inference workloads efficiently on highly efficient models like Tencent’s Hy4 flash. Over the past 12 months, inference efficiency has undergone a dramatic transformation, with token throughput on domestic chips far higher than anticipated a year ago, he said, noting that the Shenzhen-based company continues to add compute capacity through the Chinese supply chain.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: BYD Chairman Says China's Global Expansion Creates Jobs, Not Takes Them
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 18 -- Chinese manufacturers expanding overseas are creating local jobs rather than taking them away, BYD Chairman Wang Chuanfu said at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit.

"Some people outside believe that Chinese manufacturers going global means taking away local jobs, but that is not the case," Wang said at the gathering of business leaders and policymakers in Shenzhen yesterday. "What we bring are new energy vehicles, filling gaps in local markets."

BYD employs over one million people worldwide, including 60,000 overseas, the chief of the world's largest electric vehicle maker said. The company aims to bring Chinese technology to global markets while generating employment and tax revenue in the countries where it operates, he added.

BYD's factories in Thailand and Indonesia have each created nearly 6,000 local jobs, with local nationals making up at least 95 percent of their respective workforces, Wang said. The company has adopted a similar approach in Brazil.

The Chinese EV giant is also expanding local procurement and research and development to make its technology more accessible worldwide, Wang noted. In Thailand, where BYD operates a plant capable of producing 150,000 vehicles a year, its localization rate has exceeded 50 percent, with many components now sourced from local suppliers.

He pointed to Chile as another example of mutually beneficial trade. BYD buys large quantities of copper and lithium from the South American country while supplying it with electric buses that help improve the environment. "In fact, our trade is complementary," Wang said.

BYD works with 110,000 suppliers worldwide, ranging from major international companies to local businesses, Wang said, underscoring the role of global supply chains in the company's overseas expansion.

The 2026 APEC CEO Summit is taking place in Shenzhen, China, drawing more than 2,000 government and business representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including the United Kingdom and France. Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies are also attending the two-day event.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: DeepSeek Harness Releases DAU Data for First Time, Topping 1.5 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Chinese artificial intelligence giant DeepSeek has released user data for DeepSeek Harness for the first time, revealing that the open-source agent harness framework has more than 1.5 million daily active users.

DeepSeek Harness had 1.54 million DAUs on its official application programming interface over the week ended Nov. 4, up from 429,000 over the week ended Oct. 7 and 271,000 over the one ended Sept. 30, Hangzhou-based DeepSeek said yesterday. Users consume around 92 trillion tokens a day.

The number of third-party plug-ins has surged to about 35,000 since DeepSeek Harness was released, and about 60 percent of users created or installed at least one third-party plugin. It is preparing a support program for plugin authors.

DeepSeek Harness is a software support framework built around large language models, designed to help AI agents manage and execute more complex tasks. It can be seen as a complete set of operating systems an LLM needs to truly become an agent.

As a benchmark for domestic LLMs, DeepSeek is accelerating evolution. On Oct. 31, DeepSeek Harness’ team published a technical article called ‘Exploring Super-Agent Design to a More Autonomous Agent System’ on its official WeChat account.

The article claims that improved model capabilities have given rise to new applications, and personal agents have begun to emerge rapidly. However, mainstream agent design still cannot support this mode at the multi-task and team-collaboration level, and the multi-task limit depends on people’s attention.

To overcome these limitations, it is necessary to break the binding between agents and a one-off manual session, making it a continuous entity that can maintain context across sessions and simultaneously advance multiple complex tasks without interfering with each other. DeepSeek refers to this form of agent and its system architecture as ‘super-agent.’

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Private, Local Builders Step Up Land Acquisitions in Major Chinese Cities
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 18 -- Privately-held, mostly regional-based property developers are resurfacing at auctions in China’s larger cities for highly sought-after plots of land intended for housing projects, challenging the dominance of state-owned builders.

Forty-five of the 283 parcels of residential land auctioned in 32 first- and second-tier cities since September have sold at a premium, with private developers topping the bids for 21, according to statistics from Property Technology Innovation.

Private firms also accounted for seven of the 10 developers paying the highest premiums, most of which were regional players with longstanding business in their local markets, the data showed. At an auction in Nanjing, for instance, private firms battled over three much-coveted plots. After 184 rounds of bidding, Gold Pedestal Real Estate secured one at a more than 43 percent premium.

The purchases are noteworthy given that China’s real estate market has yet to come out of its prolonged slump and the industry is shifting away from a housing presale system introduced in the 1990s toward selling completed homes in accordance with new regulatory requirements.

“Not all private property developers are willing to acquire land at this stage,” Li Zimo, vice president of the Nanjing Real Estate Academy, told Yicai. “Those that do are mostly regional builders that understand the local market, have a light capital structure, and only invest in land plots at much sought-after locations or with very attractive building plans.”

Private real estate firms only commit to buying land after rigorously assessing market supply and demand, ensuring that the financial calculations make commercial sense, Li said.

Those willing to bid for land in the current climate have mostly relied on their own financial means to develop projects and have consistently maintained relatively healthy finances, according to Yu Xiaoyu, research general manager at EH Consulting.

As more private builders join up to land auctions in larger cities, the market is shifting toward one of joint participation by state-owned enterprises, which have traditionally led, and private, regional-based players, said Liu Shui, director of enterprise research at the Enterprise Research. 

“SOEs will continue to dominate in developing large projects, while private regional builders are expected to be the main buyers of small- and medium-sized land parcels in core city areas,” Liu noted.

“The adjustment of residential housing types and supporting facilities by private regional developers is often more flexible and closer to the needs of residents than that of state-owned developers, which will accelerate the evolution of products in regional markets and put competitive pressure on existing projects and non-local competitors,” Liu predicted.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Chipmaking Equipment Industry Faces Shake-Out After Players Multiply, Insiders Say
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 18 -- US-led restrictions on semiconductor equipment exports to China have hastened the growth of China’s own chipmaking equipment industry, but the resulting influx of manufacturers has created an overcrowded market ripe for consolidation, according to insiders.

Dozens of domestic firms are developing and producing key equipment for every process in the semiconductor equipment sector, with no major differences between their products, Wang Zhiyue, secretary-general of the China Electronic Production Equipment Industry Association, told Yicai. “Every type of equipment used in every process is crowded with developers,” he said.

Even in the relatively less crowded lithography machine market, there are around 10 developers, Wang noted, adding that other areas often have more than 10 or even 20 competing firms.

China’s semiconductor equipment is entering a new era of domestic substitution, Wu Kai, executive deputy secretary-general of the Semiconductor Equipment, Materials and Core Components Exhibition’s organizing committee, told Yicai.

“Opportunities are basically equal for everyone,” Wu said. “With access to capital and technological resources, anyone can start a business, creating a situation where dozens of companies compete within one product category.”

Most of these companies offer similar technology and products, making it hard to avoid cutthroat competition, Wang stressed, noting that firms use every competitive trick, such as price wars and aggressive scrambles for supply chain resources.

The homogeneity is particularly pronounced in back-end equipment, used for process such as packaging and testing, Wang said. The front-end equipment segment has higher barriers to entry and fewer overlapping offerings, thanks to massive investment and longer research and development cycles, Wang added.

Shake-Out Is Inevitable

Nevertheless, Wu said that such a phenomenon is normal at this stage. Because China’s semiconductor equipment industry has a short history, many players had to enter the space to break the foreign monopoly, Wu noted, pointing out that overseas players followed a similar development path in the past.

Signs of industry consolidation are already emerging. Naura Technology Group took a controlling stake in Kingsemi in May and began fully acquiring Beijing Nuohe Jianwei Equipment last month, while Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment bought a controlling stake in ‌Hangzhou Sizone Electronic Technology, also in May.

Consolidation is inevitable, according to Yin Zhiyao, chairman of AMEC. A fragmented, “every-man-for-himself” approach cannot succeed in this competitive landscape, he noted.

The industry’s development model will shift from the “catch-up” phase that defined the past two decades toward a focus on independent innovation over the next 20 years, Yin pointed out. The goal is not only to catch up with peers abroad, but also to surpass international state-of-the-art standards in technology and overall performance, he added.

The industry can navigate its way through the “growing pain” period over the next three to five years, Wang said. Each of the top three companies in each equipment sub-category can gain a clear competitive advantage over rivals, Wang stressed.

Semiconductor equipment mainly includes lithography machines, etching machines, thin-film deposition equipment, cleaning equipment, and packaging equipment. Each category has several sub-categories, with lithography machines the most critical gear.

Since the United States imposed export controls on advanced chips and equipment to China, leading Chinese companies such as AMEC and Naura have grown but still lag behind their overseas peers in scale and technological capabilities.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s High-Power Diesel Generator Exports to Top 6,000 in 2026 Amid AI Data Center Boom, Report Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 18 -- The global artificial intelligence data center construction boom has boosted demand for high-power compression ignition internal combustion engine generators, known as diesel generators, with China likely to export more than 6,000 units this year, the secretary-general of the China Internal Combustion Engine Industry Association told China Central Television.

China’s diesel generator market may exceed CNY10 billion (USD1.5 billion) in 2026, Jia Bin said in a report carried by CCTV yesterday. However, the supply-demand balance is expected to remain tight next year, Jia pointed out.

Exports of diesel generators rated above two megavolt-amperes, the main type used in AI data centers, reached 4,547 units in the first nine months of this year, according to data from the General Administration of Customs. In comparison, the figure stood at 3,339 units for the whole of last year.

Guangxi Yuchai Marine Power’s production lines are running at full capacity, Deputy Head of Production Jiang Yiqiang told CCTV. Orders for high-power models aimed at data centers are booked through October next year, he added.

Production capacity at leading makers of high-power diesel generators for data centers is already scheduled through 2028, according to a report from China Galaxy Securities. AI computing power is expanding exponentially, while electricity supply grows linearly, so the gap between the two keeps widening.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Changan Auto to Sell 10% Stake in EV Brand Avatr for at Least USD479.7 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- China’s Changan Automobile is seeking to sell a 10 percent stake in its electric vehicle brand Avatr Technology, which is moving ahead with a Hong Kong initial public offering amid shrinking sales and cash reserves, for a minimum of CNY3.2 billion (USD479.7 million).

Changan will list just over 306.5 million Avatr shares for sale on the Shanghai United Assets and Equity Exchange, with the disclosure period running through Dec. 10, the state-owned carmaker announced yesterday. Avatr has a valuation floor of CNY31.8 billion (USD4.8 billion), about in line with its post-money valuation after its Series C funding round in December 2024.

The buyer must pay a CNY500 million (USD75 million) deposit and settle the full purchase price within three working days of signing the equity transfer contract, Changan noted. It must also guarantee that the source of funds is legal and compliant, that the transaction will not hinder Avatr’s IPO, and that it has no competing business with the brand.

The buyer will be expected to provide support mainly in areas such as premium brand sales channel development and overseas market expansion, Changan told Yicai. After the deal closes, the Chongqing-based carmaker will continue backing Avatr in core areas including technology research and development, vehicle manufacturing, and supply chain, it added.

If the entire 10 percent stake is acquired by a single buyer, it would become Avatr’s second-largest shareholder. Changan owns about 41 percent of Avatr, making it the largest shareholder, followed by battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology with around 9.2 percent. 

Avatr sold 20,160 vehicles from January through May, according to its IPO prospectus. China Passenger Car Association data shows its domestic retail sales dropped below 3,000 last month. Its cash on hand fell to about CNY6.2 billion in late April from CNY9.7 billion on Dec. 31 and CNY19.3 billion at the end of 2024, implying an average monthly burn rate of more than CNY800 million.

For yet-to-be-profitable automakers listed in Hong Kong, sales expectations affect revenue growth and the price-to-sales ratio, while cash reserves and the cash burn rate relate to a company's cash runway, a key metric watched by capital market investors, industry experts told Yicai.

Changan’s shares [SHE: 000625] closed 0.3 percent lower at CNY6.88 (US1.03) each today, while the wider Shenzhen market shed 2.1 percent. The stock has fallen 42 percent so far this year.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chinalco Unit Deepens Grip on Vietnam's Alumina Industry With USD840 Million Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 18 -- An overseas engineering unit of Aluminum Corporation of China (Chinalco), the world's largest aluminum producer, has strengthened its foothold in Vietnam's alumina industry with a CNY5.6 billion (USD840.3 million) contract to build a new plant.

The project will add 2.4 million tons of annual alumina production capacity in Vietnam, nearly tripling the country's existing capacity of 1.3 million tons once completed, China Aluminum International Engineering Corporation announced yesterday.

Awarded by Vietnam's Binh Phuoc Ore Exploitation and Beneficiation Joint Stock Company, the contract comprises USD427 million and VND10.41 trillion (USD405.2 million). China Aluminum International Engineering will design, equip, and build the plant in southeastern Vietnam's Phuoc Binh, as well as oversee testing and defect repairs, over a 27-month period from the contract's effective date.

The Chinese company said it will recognize revenue from the CNY5.6 billion contract progressively as work advances. The project is not expected to have a significant impact on its revenue this year.

The deal adds to the company's rapidly expanding overseas business. China Aluminum International Engineering signed CNY22.1 billion (USD3.3 billion) worth of new overseas contracts in 2025, almost quadrupling from the previous year.

Despite holding an estimated 5.8 billion tons of bauxite resources, Vietnam has barely tapped its potential to develop an aluminum industry. The country produced its first electrolytic aluminum ingot only in July and has just two operating alumina plants, at Tan Rai and Nhan Co, each with an annual capacity of 650,000 tons.

China Aluminum International Engineering built both of Vietnam's existing alumina plants and is involved in nearly all of its planned capacity expansion, including the Phuoc Binh project and proposed upgrades at Tan Rai and Nhan Co. This gives the Chinese firm a pivotal role in shaping Vietnam's emerging aluminum industry, from production capacity to technical standards and operating systems.

Editor: Emmi Laine
